thread:
Alex K.: FYI — Acme Robotics asked for a Dedicated GPU pool estimate. They want a commitment discussion and an initial sizing rec for embeddings + occasional chat fallback. Can we triage?
Jordan (Sales): Context: they plan 1M embeddings/day baseline, but they expect traffic spikes. Sales asked for a plan that handles a 15-minute burst of ~4k embedding requests/min + 200 concurrent chat users during spikes. They want baseline cost estimate and a burst policy.
Priya R.: Quick clarifying q's: avg tokens per embedding? avg tokens per chat turn? target p99 latency for generation? model family? committed vs flexible burst?
Alex K.: From customer notes: avg embedding text ~300 tokens, embeddings per user ~1. Chat model usage: ~512 tokens/turn avg, up to 4 turns/session on average. They'd prefer open models (Redwood-verified embeddings model + 13B chat for cost). Target p99 for chat < 400ms if possible, embeddings p99 < 150ms. Committed pool desired with burst to shared capacity.
Sam L.: Rough mental model: 1M embeddings/day = ~11.6 qps sustained. Burst of 4k/min = ~66 qps sustained for 15 min. That sounds fine for a small pool but concurrency matters (embedding requests are short but we need batching). For embeddings we should aim for autoscale_min replic = 1-2, autoscale_max maybe 6-8 depending on GPU type.
Priya R.: What GPU types are we assuming? H100s vs A100 80GB vs A10? Also quantization — can embeddings be q4/8 to increase throughput?
Sam L.: For embeddings, a single A100-80 can typically handle ~600-1200 small-batch embedding qps (highly workload dependent). With 300-token inputs and moderate batching, an A100 80GB could handle the baseline + burst with 1-2 replicas if we tune batching. If they want lower cost, 8-bit quantized model on mixed A10s might be ok but p99 will be worse. For chat (512 tokens), a 13B quantized on A100 might handle ~20-40 concurrent streams per GPU at target latency; so 200 concurrent -> ~6 GPUs.
Jordan (Sales): They will pay for reserved capacity if we can guarantee burst shape. They asked for a canary rollout + documented fallback to hosted model when pool exhausted.
Alex K.: Proposed initial sizing (ballpark): embeddings: 2 x A100-80 (min 1 active, autoscale to 3 for sustained moderate load); chat: 6 x A100-80 (with ability to fall back to hosted instances for >6). Burst policy: allow 2x short-term burst for 15 minutes using shared pool credits; cooldown 10m.
Priya R.: That sounds reasonable. We should capture launch criteria: 1) perf test with synthetic 300-token embedding load hitting 4k/min for 15m with <=150ms p99; 2) chat perf test with 200 concurrent users, p99 <=400ms; 3) documented fallback and cost model; 4) support runbook for warm pools and pre-warming.
Sam L.: Notes for infra config (quick snippet):
```
pool_config: {
  gpu_type: "A100-80GB",
  models: ["redwood-embed-large", "redwood-chat-13b-q4f16"],
  min_replicas: 1,
  max_replicas: 8,
  target_gpu_util: 0.75,
  burst_multiplier: 2.0,
  burst_window_mins: 15,
  cooldown_mins: 10,
  prewarm_replicas: 2
}
```
Sam L.: We'll need to tune batching params: max_batch_tokens ~ 4096, prefer dynamic batching with prefix cache for chat; KV cache reuse critical for chat latency.
Alex K.: Action items: 1) Priya — confirm model family & acceptance criteria with customer (due EOD Fri). 2) Sam — run rough perf sim on staging for both embedding and chat shapes (ETA Tue). 3) Jordan — confirm commercial ask (committed months, burst allowance). 4) I'll draft the customer-facing proposal.
Priya R.: Also add metric requirements: token-level cost estimate, p50/p95/p99 latency, cold-start time, and expected billing if fallback to hosted.
Jordan (Sales): I'll get the contract ask. Customer is also interested in a short SLA for burst availability — will run by legal.
InfraBot: Perf simulation job queued (job id: perf-20261108-42). Results ETA ~48h. :gear:
Alex K.: Cool — let's sync Tue after Sam's sims. If perf looks good we prep a short runbook and pricing worksheet. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Priya R.: +1 — I'll add a checklist to the intake ticket and tag the customer for model confirmation.
Sam L.: I'll post perf logs and a follow-up thread with measured qps/latency curves.
Jordan (Sales): Thanks team. I'll loop in acct exec and solutions engineer for the commercial proposal.
